thread:
Acme Dev: Hey team - running into tool calling failures with OpenAI-compatible model. Our tool schema expects `priority: "low"|"medium"|"high"` but the model returned `"med"` and an extra top-level field `trace_id`. SDK validation throws: `InvalidEnumValue` and `UnexpectedField`. Repro below.

Acme Dev: Request (post to /v1/chat/completions):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-compat-1",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "create task"}],
  "functions": [{"name": "create_task", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"title": {"type": "string"}, "priority": {"type": "string", "enum": ["low", "medium", "high"]}}, "required": ["title"]}}]
}
```

Acme Dev: Model returned tool call (excerpt):
```json
{
  "name": "create_task",
  "arguments": "{\"title\":\"Fix login\",\"priority\":\"med\",\"trace_id\":\"abc123\"}"
}
```

Toni (Support): Thanks for the repro. Can you confirm SDK version and whether this is happening on Redwood-hosted or a customer-loaded external model? Also please paste the raw response body (not just stringified `arguments`) if you have it.

Acme Dev: Using redwood-js v0.9.2 against hosted Redwood. Raw body is same as above - `arguments` is a JSON-string (we parse it) and then we validate against our tool schema which rejects `med` and `trace_id`.

Toni (Support): Got it. Two quick asks: 1) can you run a cURL that includes the model response id so we can pull logs? 2) temporary workaround is to post-process the parsed `arguments` to map `med` -> `medium` and drop unknown top-level fields. We'll escalate to eng to investigate compatibility mode behavior.

Acme Dev: cURL with headers and response id attached:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @req.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
# response id: resp_20260315_9e7
```

incident-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4321 (P1) for toolcall schema mismatch - attaching logs.

Mira (Eng): looping in eng-ml @Raj, can you take a look? Initial hypothesis: model compatibility layer is being permissive with aliases (e.g., `med`) but our downstream SDK validator is strict. Also the model added `trace_id` for tracing - we should not treat extra fields as fatal if they’re harmless.

Raj (ML): I pulled the logs from resp_20260315_9e7. Model returned `priority: "med"` in the JSON-string arguments. Two approaches: 1) Update compatibility normalizer to accept known alias table (med -> medium) and ignore unknown top-level keys when parsing function args. 2) Add an opt-in flag in the API (e.g., `tool_compat_mode="lenient"`) so SDK validation tolerates alias enums and extra fields.

Toni (Support): Can you validate that lenient mode will not mask real schema regressions? We need a safe default.

Raj (ML): We can implement lenient mode with auditing: accept aliases/extra fields and emit a structured warning in response metadata (e.g., `compat_warnings: [{path: "arguments.priority", issue: "enum_alias", value: "med"}]`). Default remains strict; enable lenient per-request or per-tenant.

Mira (Eng): For immediate customer unblock, Toni - please share the small mapping snippet with Acme Dev so they can pre-normalize parsed args server-side. Also mark SUP-4321 for eng-ml prioritization.

Toni (Support): Acme Dev - sample JS normalizer you can add before validation:
```js
const aliasMap = { med: 'medium', lo: 'low' };
const args = JSON.parse(response.arguments);
if (args.priority && aliasMap[args.priority]) args.priority = aliasMap[args.priority];
// drop trace id
delete args.trace_id;
// then run your schema validator
```

Acme Dev: Thanks, will try and confirm. This is P1 for us since it blocks workflow creation in prod. Appreciate the quick triage.

Raj (ML): Filed internal RFC for compat-mode and alias table. Attaching examples and tests to SUP-4321.

incident-bot: SUP-4321 updated: assigned to eng-ml, priority P1.

Toni (Support): Keeping this thread open — ping us after you verify the local normalizer and we'll follow up with timeline for lenient compatibility mode in the API.

Acme Dev: Verified workaround works for now. Please keep me posted on ETA for server-side opt-in.
